For a sampled crop C, let S(C) contain the valid targets remaining after truncation and masking. With loss Σₖ∈S w(k)ℓₖ / Σⱼ∈S w(j), expected supervision exposure of original event k is E_C[1{k∈S(C)}w(k)/Σⱼ∈S(C)w(j)]. Uniform weighting gives E_C[1{k∈S(C)}/|S(C)|]. These expressions are a direct derivation from the [normalized weighted-mean reduction](https://docs.pytorch.org/rl/main/_modules/torchrl/objectives/utils.html). Exposure depends jointly on crop probability, retained targets, and the crop-specific denominator; generally it is not inclusion probability times a globally normalized weight.

If T is the full training-history length, w(k) favors absolute-event recency: weights are 1 at age zero, approximately 0.684 at age 10, 0.525 at age 30, and approach 0.5. Old-only crops therefore receive almost uniform supervision after normalization; singleton crops are exactly unchanged. Meaningful reweighting occurs when a crop contains targets with different ages near the history end. Crop selection and truncation can dominate: uniformly sampled fixed-length windows underexpose boundary events, while random endpoints followed by suffix truncation produce a different inclusion profile. Excluded targets retain zero exposure. If T instead denotes the crop endpoint, the scheme favors crop-relative recency. [Recency-sampling research](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.02643) likewise treats target selection as part of the training objective.

Analyze the actual sampler by enumeration or Monte Carlo: accumulate each retained target’s normalized loss coefficient, compare against identical crops with uniform weights, and plot exposure and exposure ratios by absolute age and history length. Report inclusion frequency separately from conditional weight, stratify by crop length, and exclude padding. This measures supervision mass, not gradient magnitude or validation improvement.
